name: Zulu
script: Latin (c, q, x for the three clicks; hl, dl and other digraphs); left to right
basis: University of Florida AFLI 2023 Beginning Zulu syllabus on Muller and Mthethwa's Sanibona I-II: greetings, introductions and kinship titles, 'I am / we are', noun classes, sounds and clicks, locatives; then question words, subject and object concords, commands, the -zo- future and negatives; then -na (have), counting, adjectives, colours and health; then food, time, possessives and relatives
src: University of Florida Africa Language Institute (AFLI), Zulu beginner syllabus 2023: weekly topics, grammar and vocabulary; textbooks Muller and Mthethwa, Sanibona I and II, and Mkhize and Nxumalo, Masikhulume isiZulu
University of Florida, SSA4905 Beginning Zulu syllabus (Fall 2020): opened, but not used for word forms because many of its forms are siSwati rather than Zulu
note: The order follows the AFLI weeks: greetings, introductions and titles, 'I am / we are', noun classes, sounds and clicks and locatives first; question words, family, concords, commands and the future next; then -na, counting, adjectives and colours, and health; then food, time and possessives. The summary I read garbled some grammar names, so every Zulu form in the titles is from my own knowledge. I moved possessives earlier (beside family, where learners need them) and placed the past tense (not named in the AFLI summary) and directions (AFLI Part Two) by my own judgment. Splitting the weeks into 24 lessons is my own.
hardest: The three clicks c, q, x (and their nasal and voiced forms), plus hl and dl
Noun classes: every noun's prefix (umu-, isi-, in-, i-) changes the words that agree with it
Concords: subject and object prefixes on the verb that match the noun class (ngiyakuthanda, siyabona)
Tone, which is not written, and long words built from many small parts

items: Sounds: five vowels, hl and dl, and b said with an inward pop
The three clicks: c, q, x, and gc, nq, ngx
Greetings: Sawubona / Sanibonani, Yebo, Unjani?, Ngiyaphila, Ngiyabonga
Leave-taking and titles: Sala kahle / Hamba kahle; baba, mama, sisi, bhuti
Introducing yourself: NginguSipho, Ngubani igama lakho?
I am / we are: ngingumfundi, singabafundi
Noun classes: umuntu / abantu, isikole / izikole, inja / izinja, igama / amagama
Places with e-…-ini, ku- and kwa-: esikoleni, endlini, eGoli, kwaZulu
Question words: Uhlala kuphi?, Uyaphi?, Wenzani?, ubani, ngani
Family: ubaba, umama, umfowethu, udadewethu, umndeni
Possessives that agree: igama lami, indlu yami, abantwana bami
Subject concords and the present: ngi-, u-, si-, ni-, ba- (ngiyafunda)
Counting and prices: kunye, kubili, kuthathu, kune, kuhlanu; Kubiza malini?
Adjectives and colours: umuntu omkhulu, inja enkulu; -mhlophe, -mnyama, -bomvu
Food and drink: ukudla, Ngicela amanzi, Ngifuna itiye
Time and days: Sithini isikhathi?, uMsombuluko, uLwesibili
